result.topic_en: The page ends a fragment on making a quartic expression a square, then gives J. A. Euler's theorem that the product of two quadratic forms of a given type is again of that form, and Lexell's problem of finding a multiplier that rationalizes a quadratic expression in a cube root, with an application to continued fractions for cube roots.
result.transcription:
490 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Analysis.
$= 5f^4\zeta^4 - 6f^3g\zeta^3\eta + 7ffgg\zeta\zeta\eta\eta - 6fg^3\zeta\eta^3 + 2g^4\eta^4,$
cujus factores sunt $(ff\zeta\zeta + gg\eta\eta)(5ff\zeta\zeta - 6fg\zeta\eta + 2gg\eta\eta)$. Quibus valoribus substitutis formula nostra quadratum reddenda fiet
$\frac{\lambda(5ff\zeta\zeta - 6fg\zeta\eta + 2gg\eta\eta)(ff\zeta\zeta + gg\eta\eta)(ff\eta\eta + hh\zeta\zeta)}{hfg\eta(2h\zeta - f\eta)},$
quae ut solubilis fiat, necesse est, ut bini superiores factores
$ff\zeta\zeta + gg\eta\eta$ et $ff\eta\eta + hh\zeta\zeta$
coalescant, quod fit ponendo $ff : hh = gg : ff$, quod sponte evenit ob $ff = -gh$, ita ut res huc redeat
$\frac{\lambda(5ff\zeta\zeta - 6fg\zeta\eta + 2gg\eta\eta)}{f\eta(f\eta - 2h\zeta)}$ vel $\frac{\lambda(5ff\zeta\zeta - 6fg\zeta\eta + 2gg\eta\eta)}{g\eta(2f\zeta + g\eta)}$,
quae iterum a praecedente non discrepat, nisi quod hic sit $f\zeta$ et $g\eta$ quod supra erat $\zeta$ et $\eta$.
A. m. T. I. p. 17 - 21.

92.
(J. A. Euler.)
Theorema. Si formula $aapp + b\beta qq$ ducatur in formulam $abrr + \alpha\beta ss$, productum erit
$aa\alpha\beta pprr + aa\alpha\beta ppss + abb\beta qqrr + ab\beta\beta qqss = ab(aapprr + \beta\beta qqss) + a\beta(\alpha appss + bbqqrr) =$
$ab(apr \pm \beta qs)^2 + a\beta(\alpha ps \mp bqr)^2.$
Hujus ergo producti forma est $abxx + a\beta yy$ existente
$x = apr \pm \beta qs$ et $y = \alpha ps \mp bqr$.
A. m. T. I. p. 130.

93.
(Lexell.)
Problema. Si fuerit $x^3 = a$ et proponatur formula $fxx + gx + h$, quaerere multiplicatorem $pxx + qx + r$, ut productum fiat numerus rationalis.
Solutio. Cum productum sit
$fpx^4 + (fq + gp)x^3 + (fr + hp + gq)xx + (gr + hq)x + hr$
ob $x^3 = a$, hoc productum reducitur ad sequentem formam
$(fr + hp + gq)xx + (fpa + gr + hq)x + fq + gp + hr = 0$
unde $r = \frac{-hp - gq}{f}$; $r = \frac{-fpa - hq}{g}$; $r = \frac{-fq - gp}{h}$
atque $hpg + g^2q = f^2pa + fhq$; $p(hg - f^2) = q(fh - g^2)$; $\frac{p}{q} = \frac{fh - gg}{hg - ff}$;
hinc $p = fh - gg$, $q = hg - ff$, $r = gf - hh$, atque productum quaesitum erit $= 3fgh - f^3 - g^3 - h^3$.
Hujus ope radices cubicas numerorum licebit ad fractiones continuas revocare. Exempl. Proponatur $x^3 = 2$, ut sit $x = \sqrt[3]{2}$; notetur esse proxime $x = 1\frac{1}{4}$ et $xx = 1\frac{1}{2}$, et nunc more consueto fractio $\frac{x}{1}$ in fractionem continuam convertatur....
A. m. T. I. p. 176.

items.english: Theorem: if the formula aapp + bβqq is multiplied by the formula abrr + αβss, the product will be ab(apr ± βqs)^2 + aβ(αps ∓ bqr)^2, i.e. of the form abxx + aβyy.

items.quote: Si fuerit $x^3 = a$ et proponatur formula $fxx + gx + h$, quaerere multiplicatorem $pxx + qx + r$, ut productum fiat numerus rationalis.
items.english: If x^3 = a and the formula fxx + gx + h is proposed, find a multiplier pxx + qx + r such that the product becomes a rational number.

items.quote: Hujus ope radices cubicas numerorum licebit ad fractiones continuas revocare.
items.english: By means of this it will be possible to reduce cube roots of numbers to continued fractions.
